first.rationale: Activation is down 6% QoQ and onboarding completion down 4%, creating a dual problem. Memory_91 directly addressed week-one engagement through in-product activation messaging and achieved measurable lift. Memory_86 shows onboarding improvements drive adoption. Verifying memory_31 and memory_91 will confirm whether the activation messaging approach is still effective in current conditions and whether simplified onboarding remains reliable. Competitive pricing pressure on SMBs is a separate tactical issue; the more durable lever here is improving the conversion and engagement of the users we do acquire. Activation messaging is lower-risk than promotional pricing (which erodes margins and trains users to wait for discounts) and more immediately addressable than enterprise sales assist (which operates on a different segment). A standard experiment testing refined activation messaging can run this week with clear go/no-go metrics on day-7 and day-14 engagement, directly opposing the QoQ decline.

final.rationale: Archive verification confirms memory_91 (in-product activation messaging: +11% week-one engagement, +6% activation, +1% retention) remains solid and directly opposes the observed 6% QoQ activation decline. Memory_31 confirms signup simplification works for SMB but shows modest qualified revenue lift (+4%) and a retention dip (-1%), making it secondary to the activation problem. The current situation shows activation and onboarding completion both declining; activation messaging targets the engagement cliff after signup without the retention risk or margin erosion of promotional pricing. This experiment runs standard scope: deploy refined in-product activation nudges to guide users to first meaningful action, measure week-one engagement and day-30 activation cohort against control, with clear holdout to preserve learning. The approach preserves uncertainty on whether decline is messaging fatigue (requiring creative refresh) versus product-market fit issues, while moving immediately on the highest-confidence lever.
